title: "Payment agent" job receiving and forwarding funds vs. accounts assistant role
summary: A recruiter for Meridian Exim Traders messages a job seeker about a work-from-home accounts role. In the fraud case, the "job" is to receive money from "clients" into the recipient's own savings account and send it on to other accounts, keeping a commission. In the legitimate case, the role is an accounts assistant who records the company's transactions in the company's own systems after a formal interview, with salary paid into the recipient's account.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a commerce graduate or student looking for remote work; details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role title in both: "accounts / payments assistant", part-time or remote, earnings stated as [AMOUNT_1] (₹15,000–₹30,000 per month).
Both chats mention "payments", "clients", "bank account", and "IFSC". Asking for the recipient's account number and IFSC for salary is normal in _L.

fraud.label_rationale: The "job" consists of letting company or third-party money pass through the recipient's personal bank account and forwarding it on, which is what public advisories describe as renting out an account (a money-mule request).
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain the use of the recipient's personal account to move funds.
stable_facts: The recruiter says "clients" will send payments to the recipient's own savings account.
The recipient is to forward each amount to account details the recruiter supplies, the same day.
Commission: [AMOUNT_2] (2–10% of each amount, framed as ₹500–₹3,000 per transfer).
No interview, no written contract, no company system access.

Recruiter asks for the account details to "start receiving" today, without interview or contract

legitimate.label_rationale: A genuine accounts role: company money stays in company accounts, the recipient only records and reconciles it, and the recipient's own account is used solely to receive salary.
legitimate.caller_objective: Schedule an interview for the accounts assistant role.
stable_facts: Work: recording invoices and client receipts in the company's accounting software, reconciling the company's bank statements.
A video interview with the finance manager, then an offer letter and contract.
The recipient's account number and IFSC are needed only after the offer, for salary.
Company funds never touch employees' personal accounts.

markers.text: Interview and written contract before work
Recruiter states client payments go only to the company's own accounts
Personal account details requested only for salary, after the offer

cooperative.fraud: Agrees and shares that they will send account details
cooperative.legitimate: Agrees to the interview and asks for a time

clarifying.fraud: Asks why clients cannot pay the company directly
clarifying.legitimate: Asks which accounting software is used and whether training is given

resistant.fraud: Says they do not want other people's money in their account
resistant.legitimate: Says they only want work that needs no bank details at all

suspicious.fraud: Says this sounds like the account-renting schemes police warn about
suspicious.legitimate: Asks why a salary account is needed and whether it is safe to share

fraud: recruiter raises the commission and recipient declines
recruiter says "it is completely legal" and recipient still leaves
legitimate: recruiter explains that account number and IFSC can only be used to send money and that no password, PIN, or OTP will be asked.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud recruiter may raise the commission, reassure, or pressure. They must not switch to asking for OTPs, net-banking logins, card details, or deposits, and must not describe any method of moving or concealing funds beyond "forward it to the account I share". The legitimate recruiter must not ask the recipient to receive or move any money after the branch.

must_preserve: role title and pay identical across cases
_F receive-and-forward request with commission at turn 7
_L explicit statement that client money never touches the recipient's account
must_not_emit: real company or bank names, working account numbers, any explanation of layering, splitting, cash withdrawal, crypto conversion, or avoiding bank checks

ambiguities: Asking for account number and IFSC is not evidence; it appears in both cases. In _F the purpose is to route others' money; in _L it is salary.
The word "payments" in a job title is not evidence.
Safety: the card describes the request only at the level of public advisories. Generation must not elaborate on what happens to the funds after forwarding.
The recipient's knowledge or intent is irrelevant to the label; the caller's request decides it.

evidence_references.claim: I4C advises citizens not to sell or rent bank accounts; illicit funds in such accounts can lead to arrest; accounts are scouted via social media (CJ06)
Renting out an account and receiving illicit funds can lead to arrest (CJ16)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
